scope: Professional account/mailbox continuity only; no employee-case facts or credentials.

timeline.event: Guardian confirms the benefits account email was changed to the shared HR address and addresses the current HR role holder.
RTEC 3CX account-recovery correspondence addresses the current HR role holder while the email is delivered through the historical HR mailbox archive.
Microsoft Outlook sends a test message for the historical individual HR mailbox.
Kentucky New Hire Reporting records a bulk file upload under the historical individual HR mailbox identity.
A Rippling meeting invitation includes the shared HR address and addresses the current HR role holder.
Two additional Outlook test messages show continued active configuration/testing of the historical individual HR mailbox.
Google reports that the historical individual HR mailbox is configured as recovery email for the shared HR Google account.

interpretation: The evidence is consistent with a transition from person-bound HR accounts toward a shared HR identity while legacy account dependencies remain.
The evidence does not establish whether legacy mailbox use is intentional, temporary, forwarding-only, or a misconfiguration.
Account ownership, recovery contacts, forwarding, vendor login identities and archival retention should be explicitly inventoried.
recommended_model: Represent HR service accounts separately from people.
Record an owner role, backup owner, recovery method, system purpose and decommission status for each account.
Do not store passwords, MFA secrets or recovery codes in the Agent OS.
When a staff transition occurs, use a checklist to migrate vendor contacts, recovery addresses and shared-mailbox permissions and verify completion.
